statement: Each side of a triangle is 4 cm long. An ant walks all the way round the edge of the triangle two times. How far does the ant walk?

choices.misconception: I gave the length of one side, not the whole walk.
I walked along one side two times instead of all the way round two times.
I found the distance once round the triangle and forgot that the ant goes round two times.
I thought a triangle has 4 sides, like a square, so once round is 16 cm.

hints: How far is it once all the way round?
The distance all the way round a shape is all its sides added together. A triangle has 3 sides. Find the distance once round, then think about twice round.

solutions.reliable: Once round the triangle is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 cm. Twice round is 12 + 12 = 24 cm. The idea to keep: find the distance once round first, then repeat it.
solutions.elegant: Going round twice means walking along 6 sides of 4 cm each: 6 x 4 = 24 cm. The idea to keep: count all the sides walked.

whyOnTest: Perimeter: the distance round a shape adds every side, and stopping after one side or one lap is the usual mistake.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
